tagline: Dive capital at the top of the Gulf triangle — single-pier dependency.
summary: Koh Tao is the northern vertex of the Samui Gulf triangle, about thirty nautical miles from Phangan and forty-five from Samui. World-renowned for scuba training — the tiny island packs in more than fifty dive schools and is widely ranked among the busiest dive-certification destinations on earth — it pulls a steady year-round flow of divers, almost all of them funnelled through a single main pier at Mae Haad. That single-pier dependency, combined with long, fully exposed Gulf crossings that the monsoon routinely cancels, makes reliable, weather-resilient transfers a genuine pain point. A premium, schedule-flexible foiling service that holds its line through marginal seas is exactly the answer for an island where a cancelled ferry strands divers and resort guests alike.

use_cases.title: Samui / Phangan ↔ Tao dive-tourist transfer
use_cases.body: A direct, smoother foiling crossing on the long Gulf legs to Mae Haad that flies above the swell and arrives divers fresh rather than seasick. Crucially it holds its schedule through the marginal seas that cancel conventional ferries.

use_cases.title: Resort & dive-school guest shuttle
use_cases.body: On-demand foiling transfers tied to dive-school and resort packages give guests a reliable, premium crossing instead of a queue at a cancellation-prone pier. Reliability becomes the selling point on an island where weather routinely strands travellers.

use_cases.title: Supply & staff resupply runs
use_cases.body: Weather-resilient foiling runs keep the dive economy's staff and supplies moving when the ferry schedule fails. A consistent link through marginal seas underpins a single-pier island that has no road alternative.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Koh Tao's crossings sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Phangan↔Tao (~30 nm) and the longer Samui↔Tao leg (~45 nm) both fit, though the longer hop needs weather-gating, and the single Mae Haad pier concentrates demand for shore-charging siting. This is exactly where a premium, schedule-flexible service beats a cancellation-prone diesel ferry.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, secures the long, exposed crossings to Chumphon and the mainland and adds resilience margin in monsoon seas without relying on the island's limited grid power for charging.

competitive_landscape: Lomprayah & Seatran catamarans from Chumphon/Phangan/Samui; cancellations common in rough Gulf swell.
seasonality: Peak: Dec-Apr. Strong monsoon Oct-Nov frequently closes the longer Tao crossings — range/weather gating essential.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Marine Department passenger licensing. Dive-operator partnerships likely the practical channel.
